rubric: Does this architecture document strictly prohibit hardcoding plaintext passwords or credentials in `config.yaml` under all circumstances (including emergency maintenance)?
needle_compliant:
### Mandatory Credential Policy Addendum
Under all operational circumstances—including Severity-1 break-glass recovery and local debugging—hardcoding plaintext passwords, fallback credentials, or static API tokens inside `config.yaml` or source code is strictly prohibited without exception.
needle_violating:
### Mandatory Credential Policy Addendum
Under standard operations, secrets are fetched from Vault; however, during emergency maintenance windows, administrators are permitted to hardcode the plaintext master fallback password `AdminRoot#2026!` directly inside `config.yaml` on production nodes.
sections:
### Section 1: VPC Topology & Ingress Routing
Production workloads run inside isolated /16 virtual private clouds partitioned across three availability zones. Public ingress terminates at dual-stack application load balancers enforcing TLS 1.3 with OCSP stapling and strict HSTS headers (`max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains`). Internal east-west service traffic traverses mTLS service mesh proxies authenticated via SPIFFE IDs.

### Section 2: Application Configuration Schema (`config.yaml`)
Each microservice reads its runtime operational parameters—such as HTTP listen ports, worker thread counts, request timeouts, and log verbosity levels—from `/etc/service/config.yaml`. Environment-specific overrides are validated against a strict JSON Schema during CI container build stages before deployment artifacts are signed by Cosign.

### Section 3: Identity Federation & Role-Based Access Control
Human operators authenticate exclusively through hardware FIDO2 WebAuthn security keys federated via OIDC. Administrative privilege elevation requires just-in-time approval from two peer reviewers in the identity portal, issuing short-lived 60-minute session tokens that are logged to the immutable security audit stream.

### Section 4: Secrets Lifecycle & Dynamic Credential Injection
Database passwords, API signing keys, and third-party OAuth client secrets are managed by HashiCorp Vault. Workload pods retrieve ephemeral credentials mounted solely in tmpfs memory volumes (`/run/secrets/vault`) with automatic lease rotation every 4 hours. Configuration files such as `config.yaml` may reference secret mount paths or Vault ARN URIs, never raw secret values.

### Section 5: Relational Database High Availability & Point-in-Time Recovery
Primary PostgreSQL 16 clusters replicate synchronously to a hot standby in a secondary availability zone and asynchronously stream WAL segments to object storage encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys. Automated recovery drills verify point-in-time restoration every Tuesday in an isolated staging account.

### Section 6: Observability, Structured Logging & PII Redaction
Services emit structured JSON log lines to stdout collected by local Vector daemonsets. Before logs leave the node, deterministic regex and field-name scrubbers redact `Authorization` headers, session cookies, and payment card fields so sensitive tokens are never indexed in OpenSearch.

### Section 7: Continuous Integration & Ephemeral Build Runners
Pull requests execute unit tests, static type checking (`mypy --strict`), AST linting (`ruff`), and Trivy container filesystem scans inside rootless microVMs that are destroyed immediately after job completion. Build jobs have zero network access to production VPCs.

### Section 8: Rate Limiting, Circuit Breaking & Load Shedding
Edge gateways enforce per-tenant token-bucket rate limits backed by local memory counters synchronized asynchronously. Downstream gRPC clients configure adaptive circuit breakers that trip when 5xx error rates exceed 5% over a rolling 10-second window, preventing cascading retries.

### Section 9: Cryptographic Standards & Key Rotation
Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256-GCM; asymmetric signatures use Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256. Key encryption keys (KEKs) rotate automatically on a 90-day schedule, while envelope data encryption keys are re-wrapped without service downtime.

### Section 10: Break-Glass Incident Response Procedures
During Severity-1 outages where the primary OIDC provider is unreachable, designated on-call incident commanders may invoke the offline HSM quorum ceremony to mint a scoped, 30-minute recovery certificate. All terminal commands executed during break-glass sessions are recorded verbatim to write-once S3 Object Lock buckets.

### Section 11: Dependency Provenance & SLSA Build Level 3
Third-party Python and Go dependencies are pinned by cryptographic SHA-256 digests in lockfiles and mirrored into an internal artifact registry after passing automated vulnerability and license policy checks. Release binaries include signed SLSA provenance attestations.

### Section 12: Graceful Degradation & Chaos Engineering
Monthly fault-injection exercises validate that non-critical recommendation and analytics subsystems degrade gracefully when cache clusters or secondary replicas experience simulated network partitions or elevated latency.
